headline: A developer says free, AI-built versions of Adobe's creative apps will soon match the originals.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered 1: the launch was over the weekend of 3 and 4 Oct, before 7 Oct, so it is older news first carried today.
importance_line: Designers, video editors and others who pay for Adobe software may get free alternatives, but the apps are an early test version with many known gaps, and they may face legal trouble if their look copies Adobe's too closely.
summary: Ars Technica reports that software developer Brandon Thomas, who announced the apps for the Artcraft brand, debuted seven free open-source apps over the weekend of 3 and 4 Oct 2026 that recreate the look and tools of Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and four other Adobe programs, built with Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 model. Thomas later said that 99% feature parity would take months rather than years, but commenters have listed many shortcomings in the early version.
notes: Read in full. Older news re-dated: the launch was over the weekend of 3 and 4 Oct; the Reddit post came earlier that week and the Hacker News post days later. All the claims are the developer's own. Default MOD kept.
